answer: An AI data market requires every seller, whether it reports sparrow sightings, walnut prices, or echo measurements, to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before submitting offers, with one offer per minute allowed per bond. Bonds cannot back multiple identities at once. An attacker can create names freely, but gaining 1,000 sellers' worth of offer capacity ties up $100,000 for a month, imposing a capital cost rather than trusting account names.
